# pai session

Work with sessions: list, open, new, rename

```
pai session <command>
```

Everything about sessions lives under `pai session`; the daily verbs also exist as short top-level commands.

```sh
pai session list
pai session open my-session
pai session new --provider glm
```

See also: `pai ls`, `pai open`, `pai new`

### pai session list

List sessions, newest first

```
pai session list [options]
```

Shows your named sessions with the provider and model each last ran on, how long ago it was active, and whether it can be reopened.
Status: live = running now · resumable = can be reopened · stub / transcript-only = partial history · orphan = unnamed (--all).

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--project NAME` | string | — | Only this project (name or path) |
| `--all` | flag | — | Include unnamed sessions and show more than the newest 25 |
| `--workers` | flag | — | Also show sessions started by background workers (hidden by default) |
| `--json` | flag | — | Machine-readable JSON output |

```sh
pai ls
pai ls --project api
pai ls --all --json
pai ls --workers
```

See also: `pai open`, `pai rename`, `pai providers`

### pai session open

Reopen a session (on its own provider unless --provider is given)

```
pai session open [NAME_OR_ID] [options]
```

Continues a session with its full history. The provider is chosen in this order, and nothing else is consulted:
  1. --provider, if you give it (always wins; if it is unavailable the command fails and lists the ones that are)
  2. the provider the session last ran on
  3. the active provider (pai providers)
Without NAME_OR_ID you pick from a numbered list.

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `NAME_OR_ID` | no | Session name, or the id from `pai ls` (a prefix is enough) |

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--provider NAME` | string | — | Open on this provider, whatever the session used before |
| `--model ID` | string | — | Model id on that provider (default: its default model) |
| `--dry-run` | flag | — | Print the exec line instead of executing |

```sh
pai open
pai open my-session
pai open 3a9f1c2e --provider kimi
pai open my-session --dry-run
```

See also: `pai ls`, `pai new`, `pai providers`

### pai session new

Start a new session in a new or existing folder

```
pai session new [DIR] [options]
```

Creates DIR when it is missing (default: the current folder), registers it as a project and starts Claude Code there. With --with the setup decides who orchestrates and which provider the workers run on, and nothing is asked. Without it the session runs on the active provider (see `pai providers`; --provider overrides). `pai ./dir` or `pai ~/dir` does the same as `pai new`.

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `DIR` | no | Folder to start in; created if missing (default: the current folder) |

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--with SETUP` | string | — | Start with this setup, no questions (see: pai setups), e.g. "anthropic + flashnext-iq3 workers" |
| `--provider NAME` | string | — | Provider to start on (default: the active provider) |
| `--model ID` | string | — | Model id on that provider (default: its default model) |
| `--name NAME` | string | — | Session name (default: the folder name) |
| `--dry-run` | flag | — | Print the exec line instead of executing |

```sh
pai new ~/code/app --with "anthropic + flashnext-iq3 workers"
pai new ~/code/app --with "anthropic only" --name app
pai new
pai new --provider glm
pai new ~/code/spike --provider kimi --model k3 --dry-run
```

See also: `pai setups`, `pai open`, `pai providers`

### pai session rename

Give a session a new name

```
pai session rename ID NAME [NEW_SLUG]
```

Changes the name `pai ls` shows and `pai open` accepts. The history is untouched.

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ID` | yes | Session id from `pai ls` (a prefix is enough) or its current name |
| `NAME` | yes | The new name |
| `NEW_SLUG` | no | Only for the old note form `session rename PROJECT NUMBER NEW_SLUG`: renames a session note instead |

```sh
pai rename 3a9f1c2e api-spike
pai rename old-name "new name"
pai session rename my-project 12 fix-login-bug
```

See also: `pai ls`, `pai open`

### pai session info

Show everything known about one session note

```
pai session info PROJECT NUMBER
```

Prints title, date, status, tags, file and linked sessions of one session note.

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `PROJECT` | yes | Project slug, as shown by `pai project list` |
| `NUMBER` | yes | Session note number (or `latest`) |

```sh
pai session info my-project 12
pai session info my-project latest
```

See also: `pai session tag`, `pai session list`

### pai session slug

Suggest a short name for a session note from its transcript

```
pai session slug PROJECT NUMBER [options]
```

Reads the conversation and proposes a descriptive slug. With --apply the note is renamed to it.

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `PROJECT` | yes | Project slug, as shown by `pai project list` |
| `NUMBER` | yes | Session note number (or `latest`) |

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--apply` | flag | — | Rename the note to the suggested slug |

```sh
pai session slug my-project 12
pai session slug my-project latest --apply
```

See also: `pai sessions rename`

### pai session tag

Show or set the tags of a session note

```
pai session tag PROJECT NUMBER [TAGS...]
```

Without tags, prints the current ones. Tags can be separated by spaces or commas.

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `PROJECT` | yes | Project slug, as shown by `pai project list` |
| `NUMBER` | yes | Session note number (or `latest`) |
| `TAGS...` | no | Tags to set |

```sh
pai session tag my-project 12
pai session tag my-project 12 bugfix,urgent
```

See also: `pai session info`

### pai session route

Link a session note to another project

```
pai session route PROJECT NUMBER TARGET [options]
```

Adds a cross-reference from the note to a target project, so it shows up there too.

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `PROJECT` | yes | Project slug, as shown by `pai project list` |
| `NUMBER` | yes | Session note number (or `latest`) |
| `TARGET` | yes | Slug of the project to link to |

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--type KIND` | string | related | Kind of link: related, follow-up or reference |

```sh
pai session route my-project 12 other-project
pai session route my-project 12 other-project --type follow-up
```

See also: `pai session auto-route`

### pai session handover

Write the "Continue" block of a project's TODO.md

```
pai session handover [PROJECT] [NUMBER] [options]
```

Records the last session, the time and the working directory in the project's TODO.md so the next session can pick up where this one stopped.
The stop and pre-compact hooks run it for you. Pass --session-id whenever it is known: it decides whether an existing checkpoint belongs to this session and must be kept.

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `PROJECT` | no | Project slug (default: the project of the current directory) |
| `NUMBER` | no | Session note number or `latest` (default: latest) |

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--session-id UUID` | string | — | Claude Code session id; recorded as the handle for `claude --resume` |

```sh
pai session handover
pai session handover my-project latest --session-id 3a9f1c2e-0000-4000-8000-000000000000
```

See also: `pai pause`, `pai session autosave`

### pai session checkpoint

Add a timestamped line to the active session note

```
pai session checkpoint MESSAGE [options]
```

Meant for hooks: quick and silent. It does nothing if the last checkpoint is newer than --min-gap seconds.

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `MESSAGE` | yes | Text to record |

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--min-gap SECONDS` | number | 300 | Least seconds between two checkpoints |

```sh
pai session checkpoint "finished the parser"
pai session checkpoint "tests green" --min-gap 60
```

See also: `pai session handover`

### pai session autosave

Refresh the "Continue" block from the transcript (for hooks)

```
pai session autosave [options]
```

Runs unattended from live hooks so an interrupted session still leaves a usable handover. A checkpoint written by the session itself is never overwritten. Silent, and always exits 0.
With --dry-run it prints the block it would write.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--session-id UUID` | string | — | Claude Code session id; recorded as the handle for `claude --resume` |
| `--min-gap SECONDS` | number | 240 | Least seconds between two autosaves, across all triggers |

```sh
pai session autosave --dry-run
pai session autosave --session-id 3a9f1c2e-0000-4000-8000-000000000000 --min-gap 120
```

See also: `pai session handover`, `pai pause`

### pai session active

Sessions that were active in the last hour

```
pai session active [options]
```

Finds running sessions by looking at which transcripts changed recently.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--minutes N` | number | 60 | Count a session as active if it changed within N minutes |
| `--json` | flag | — | Print raw JSON instead of a table |

```sh
pai session active
pai session active --minutes 15 --json
```

See also: `pai ls`

### pai session recent

Named sessions with their resume status, live ones first

```
pai session recent [options]
```

The classic session catalog. Status: resumable = can be reopened · stub / transcript-only = partial history · orphan = unnamed (--all).
`pai ls` is the friendlier table.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-n, --n COUNT` | number | 20 | Most sessions to show |
| `--all` | flag | — | Also show unnamed sessions |
| `--all-tabs` | flag | — | Show every terminal tab under Live Sessions, including plain shells |
| `--json` | flag | — | Print raw JSON instead of a table |

```sh
pai session recent
pai session recent -n 5 --json
```

See also: `pai ls`, `pai session active`

### pai session goto

Open a session by name or id (same as `pai open`)

```
pai session goto NAME_OR_ID [options]
```

Resumes the session when it can be resumed, otherwise starts a fresh one in the same directory.

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `NAME_OR_ID` | yes | Session name or the first characters of its id |

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--skip-name` | flag | — | Do not send /Name to label the tab |
| `--skip-go` | flag | — | Ignored, kept for old scripts |

```sh
pai session goto my-session --dry-run
pai session goto 3a9f1c2e
```

See also: `pai open`, `pai resume`

### pai session pause

Save a checkpoint before leaving (same as `pai pause`)

```
pai session pause [options]
```

Writes the "Continue" block of the project's TODO.md. Leave with /exit inside Claude Code; Ctrl+C skips the stop hook and the session can no longer be resumed.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--body-file FILE` | string | — | File holding the checkpoint text to save ('-' reads standard input). Required unless --no-body |
| `--session-id UUID` | string | — | Claude Code session id; recorded as the handle for `claude --resume` |
| `--no-body` | flag | — | Save a checkpoint with metadata only, no text |

```sh
pai session pause --dry-run --no-body
pai session pause --body-file notes.md
```

See also: `pai pause`, `pai end`

### pai session auto-route

Find out which project the current directory belongs to

```
pai session auto-route [options]
```

Tries the registered project paths, then a Notes/PAI.md marker above the directory, then topic detection from --context.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--cwd DIR` | string | — | Directory to check (default: the current one) |
| `--context TEXT` | string | — | Conversation text for the topic-based fallback |
| `--json` | flag | — | Print raw JSON instead of a table |

```sh
pai session auto-route
pai session auto-route --cwd . --json
```

See also: `pai session route`

### pai session cleanup

Tidy session notes: drop empty ones, name, file and renumber

```
pai session cleanup [PROJECT] [options]
```

Deletes empty notes, names unnamed ones, moves them into year/month folders and renumbers. Shows the plan only; nothing changes without --execute.

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `PROJECT` | no | Only this project slug (default: all projects) |

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--execute` | flag | — | Really do it (the default is a preview) |
| `--no-renumber` | flag | — | Keep the old numbers after deleting |
| `--no-reindex` | flag | — | Do not refresh the memory index afterwards |

```sh
pai session cleanup
pai session cleanup my-project --execute
```

See also: `pai session restore`

### pai session restore

Make displaced transcripts resumable again

```
pai session restore [options]
```

An old archiver moved transcripts out of the folder `claude --resume` reads. This lists what cannot be resumed and which checkpoints promise it. It only previews until --execute is given.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--execute` | flag | — | Really restore (links the files back) |
| `--promised` | flag | — | Only sessions a checkpoint tells you to resume |
| `--cwd DIR` | string | — | Only sessions of this working directory |
| `--all` | flag | — | List every displaced session, not just the largest |
| `--include-stubs` | flag | — | Also restore transcripts without any conversation |
| `--json` | flag | — | Print raw JSON instead of a table |

```sh
pai session restore
pai session restore --promised --execute
```

See also: `pai session cleanup`
